RT by @no_itsmyturn: Saudi Arabia announced the establishment of the Multinational Maritime Defense Alliance, to protect freedom of navigation and secure global energy supply routes in the Bab el-Mandeb Strait, the Red Sea, and the Gulf of Aden. In a joint statement signed by 14 of the participating countries in the alliance’s founding meeting, the countries committed to strengthen cooperation in the areas of maritime security, information and intelligence sharing, operational planning, joint exercises, and the execution of joint maritime operations aimed at enhancing maritime security. Saudi Arabia will be considered the leading state of the Coalition and its permanent headquarters. “The founding states affirm that the establishment of this multinational maritime defense coalition represents a strategic step towards enhancing maritime security in the Bab el-Mandeb Strait, the Red Sea, and the Gulf of Aden, consolidating defense cooperation among member states, and supporting stability and prosperity,” the statement said. As part of the results of this meeting, 14 of the participating countries issued a joint statement in which they confirmed their support for the multinational naval defense alliance project, and welcomed the agreement reached regarding its founding arrangements, namely: Saudi Arabia 🇸🇦, Kuwait 🇰🇼, Bahrain 🇧🇭, Qatar 🇶🇦, Pakistan 🇵🇰, Turkey 🇹🇷, Egypt 🇪🇬, Jordan 🇯🇴, the Republic of Yemen 🇾🇪, Bangladesh 🇧🇩, Nigeria 🇳🇬, Sudan 🇸🇩, Djibouti 🇩🇯, and Somalia 🇸🇴. “Other countries participating in the meeting also confirmed their support for the initiative, and are in the process of completing their internal national procedures and approvals necessary to join the joint statement, and the door to joining this statement will remain open to them and to the other willing countries, after completing their national procedures,” the statement said. It should be noted that some countries whose Chiefs-of-Staff met today in Riyadh as part of the coalition meeting (in the picture) aren’t mentioned in this statement. Countries such as the U.S., Morocco and New Zealand.
